subject: assign bootstrap sample weights in boostrapLavaan?

messages.author: 93a768cdebfde0f1
messages.subject: assign bootstrap sample weights in boostrapLavaan?
parts:
Hello,
    Forgive me if I am simply overlooking an obvious reason why this would not work (or would produce wonky results), but is there any reason why it would be problematic for me to modify the boostrapLavaan code to assign sampling probabilities in the call to sample() within boostrapLavaan()?. For instance, modifying:

###Original

fn <- function(b) {
if(type == "bollen.stine" || type == "ordinary" || type == "yuan") {
# take a bootstrap sample for each group
for(g in 1:lavsamplestats@ngroups) {
stopifnot(lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]] > 1L)
boot.idx <- sample(x=lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]],
size=lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]], replace=TRUE)
dataX[[g]] <- dataX[[g]][boot.idx,,drop=FALSE]
if(!is.null(dataeXo[[g]]))
dataeXo[[g]] <- dataeXo[[g]][boot.idx,,drop=FALSE]
}
} else { # parametric!
for(g in 1:lavsamplestats@ngroups) {
dataX[[g]] <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]],
Sigma = Sigma.hat[[g]],
mu = Mu.hat[[g]])
}
}


to be:

###MODIFIED

fn <- function(b) {
if(type == "bollen.stine" || type == "ordinary" || type == "yuan") {
# take a bootstrap sample for each group
for(g in 1:lavsamplestats@ngroups) {
stopifnot(lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]] > 1L)
boot.idx <- sample(x=lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]],
size=lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]], replace=TRUE,prob = VECTOR.OF.PROBABILITIES)
dataX[[g]] <- dataX[[g]][boot.idx,,drop=FALSE]
if(!is.null(dataeXo[[g]]))
dataeXo[[g]] <- dataeXo[[g]][boot.idx,,drop=FALSE]
}
} else { # parametric!
for(g in 1:lavsamplestats@ngroups) {
dataX[[g]] <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]],
Sigma = Sigma.hat[[g]],
mu = Mu.hat[[g]])
}
} 

Thanks in advance for the input.

-tyler

messages.subject: Re: assign bootstrap sample weights in boostrapLavaan?
parts:
Have you read http://amstat.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01621459.1988.10478591?
This might help, too:
http://web.missouri.edu/~kolenikovs/talks/svy_bstrap_ce_course.pdf
(pops us when you google Rao and Wu 1988 bootstrap; no self-promotion
whatsoever :) ). tl;dr: there are complications if you have complex
survey samples that go beyond just sticking weights somewhere. Even if
this works in terms of producing *something* in the output, the
numbers could be, as you put it, "wonky".
